A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JDCL research, with matching core formulations and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original JDCL results on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100, including continual classification, semi-supervised learning, component ablations, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original JDCL experiments and adds ImageNet100 results, expanded ablations, generative-quality measurements, runtime comparisons, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The main JDCL procedure and losses remain unchanged. Appendix G adds an evaluated architectural alternative that chains attention over UNet representations instead of pooling them. This extends the examined model variants without replacing the main pooling-based method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates CIFAR10 and CIFAR100; v3 additionally evaluates five-task ImageNet100, described as 120,000 training images at 64×64 resolution. This materially extends coverage beyond the original CIFAR collections while retaining their supervised and semi-supervised scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds EWC, GKD (LwF), MKD (iCaRL), TKD (SS-IL), and ANCL to the existing CIFAR comparisons. Figure 6 adds supervised representation baselines SL, SL+MLP, t-ReX, and SupCon. Conversely, Table 2 removes the semi-supervised oEWC row. These changes substantially broaden the comparator families.

E3.justification: Figure 1 changes from first-task CIFAR100 training for 110 epochs to CIFAR10 training for 100,000 steps with similarly sized models and additional distillation controls. Appendix B revises stated training budgets, including CIFAR10's initial local training from 60,000 to 50,000 steps. New evaluations introduce generative-quality and transfer metrics, controlled A100 runtime comparisons, and reduced-precision training. These reported changes do not establish that retained scores were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds separate removal of knowledge distillation and two-stage training, previously untested individually. New analyses examine logit-distribution alignment, component behavior across tasks, attention versus pooling, transfer, training loss versus runtime, and sensitivity to β. The earlier representation-drift and UMAP analyses are retained as Figures 7 and 8 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 Section 5.1 explicitly states that evaluated metrics are averaged over three seeds and reported with standard deviations. v3 retains mean±deviation entries but removes this general statement, explicitly documenting three-seed averaging only for Figure 1. This changes reporting scope without establishing an increase or decrease in actual runs.

E6.justification: The main CIFAR JDCL accuracy values remain 83.69, 47.95, and 29.04. v3 adds substantial results, including ImageNet100 accuracy of 54.53±2.15 versus GUIDE's 39.07±1.37, new ablations, and generative-quality, runtime, transfer, and sensitivity measurements. Table 3 changes the full-model entry from 83.3 to 83.7. Figure 1 reports replacement results under changed conditions, not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The class-incremental assumptions, joint probability factorization, and denoising, classification, distillation, and semi-supervised loss formulations remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and the added empirical metrics introduce no substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about joint modeling, generative replay, semi-supervised learning, and useful representations are retained. v3 elevates reduced computational cost into an explicit introductory contribution and attributes performance gains to higher-quality rehearsal samples. The principal method contribution and conclusion remain stable.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations connecting logit alignment to distillation, generation precision to classifier performance, and weak classification signals to semi-supervised CIFAR100 difficulties. It also discusses attention's classification–generation tradeoff and two-stage training's stability–plasticity tradeoff. v1's explicit qualification that the method costs more than buffer-based approaches is removed, although generative replay's computational burden remains discussed.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the hidden-for-review code reference with a repository URL and adds model sizes, ResNet152 details for Figure 1, ResNet18 for separate-model ablations, ImageNet100 implementation information, and runtime methodology. It also clarifies initialization from the current global model. Conversely, v1's detailed CPU/GPU specifications and total research-compute estimates are removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for ImageNet, complementary networks, supervised continual representation learning, exemplar-free distillation, and DER transfer measurements. Two-stage training is more explicitly connected to prior approaches. The existing related-work taxonomy and overall positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Much of the abstract, related work, background, method exposition, and conclusion is retained. Targeted rewrites clarify the motivating experiment and local-to-global training, formalize the introductory pseudocode, and reorganize supplementary sections. The representation-stability discussion moves into the appendix; much of the additional prose accompanies new scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with a step axis and four curves; the main accuracy/forgetting table is reorganized across main-text and supplementary displays. New mechanism plots, an attention diagram, expanded comparison charts, and numerous additional tables substantially change the visual organization.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important evidential gaps: Table 3 separately tests distillation and two-stage training, Figure 6 adds supervised representation comparators, and ImageNet100 plus generative-quality analyses substantially broaden validation. These gains outweigh the loss of some uncertainty and compute disclosures. Efficiency claims still require qualification: Table 5 reports standard JDCL at 53.83 GPU-hours versus GUIDE's 30.60; the lower cost applies to JDCL (fast), at 27.21 hours.
